title: Integrated Learning and Robust Optimization
summary: Many operational decisions require solving a linear program whose cost vector is unknown at decision time and must be predicted from contextual information. Because prediction and decision are only weakly aligned, the emerging integrated learning and optimization (ILO) paradigm trains the predictor through the downstream problem, judging a prediction by the decision it induces. However, predictions are inevitably imprecise, so robustness often enters the decision stage.
